messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: scale_shape question
parts:
You could use the filled shapes (21-25) and the use a fill scale where
one of the fill colors is NA.:

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=mpg)) +
geom_point(aes(shape=factor(vs), fill=factor(am))) +
scale_shape_manual(values=c(21, 22)) +
scale_fill_manual(values=c(NA, "black"))

For a list of point shapes:
http://wiki.stdout.org/rcookbook/Graphs/Shapes%20and%20line%20types/

-Winston

On Wed, Aug 29, 2012 at 12:07 PM, Tom A. <ande...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hello all,
> I am attempting to create a scatterplot where I want to show two different
> factors simultaneously, with four (Dens.AMAN in code below) and two
> (Dens.AMMA) levels of each factor, respectively. I was hoping to do this
> using four symbols that can be either open or closed (e.g. circle, square,
> triangle, diamond). Is there a way to specify a subset of data points
> within shape_solid() to become open or closed? Or would this be done more
> simply in scale_shape_manual()? Any help or advice on where to look would
> be greatly appreciated.
>
> ggplot(test1,aes(AMAN.surv,Mean.SVL))+geom_point(aes(size=2,shape=as.factor(Dens.AMMA)))+
>
> stat_smooth(method="lm",color="black",aes(lty=as.factor(Dens.AMMA)))+theme_bw()+scale_shape(solid=F)+
> opts(panel.grid.major = theme_line(colour=NA ),panel.grid.minor =
> theme_line(colour = NA))
>
> Cheers,
> Tom

parts:
Revisiting this one because I realized there was a problem with the legend. In the code I supplied previously, the legend for fill used the default point shape, 16. This point shape only usees 'colour' and not 'fill', and so both points in the legend are black.

Here's a fixed version. It uses guide_legend to specify the shape used in the legend. (I also changed the shapes to make them easier to distinguish.)
